text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed with nearby positions reversing their earlier upward move to end at the day's lows. Distant months were higher in thin volume. May lost $0.60 to close at $306.10 per tonne, while August gave up $0.40 to close at $305.90 per tonne. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Raw sugar futures in New York settled weaker and near the day's lows after mixed selling emerged late in the session.

Cyclone Justin's recent damage to the sugar cane crop in Australia failed to inspire speculative activity as, given an ample harvest this year, the damage is unlikely to affect prices. The Australian Cane Growers Industry Association recently said that at least 20 per cent of the country's once-expected 38-40 million tonnes of 1997/98 sugar cane had been seriously hit by Justin. However, Hong Kong traders said, that reports on the impact of Cyclone Justin on the Australian crop were exaggerated, which would be normal practice. March lost 6 points to close at 10.86 cents/lb, while July shed 4 points to close at 10.63 cents/lb. The outer months closed unchanged to 4 points lower.

EUROPE - Rainfall in Europe was below normal in March in many regions but soil moisture supplies are mainly adequate at this point. Temperatures were above normal in the first half of March while cooler temperatures set in during the second half, which slowed sugar beet sowings in some areas. In the UK 68 percent of the crop was already in the ground during the week ended March 23 compared with 30 percent at the same stage last year. The total sugar beet area is expected to remain unchanged from last year at 170,000 ha.

SWITZERLAND - After a record domestic harvest in 1996/97 which yielded 203,000 tonnes raw value, sugar imports continue to fall. Overall shipments in January 1997 reached 7,405 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from last year's 14,341 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (October/January) to 39,302 tonnes against 56,219 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 169,593 tonnes compared to 155,620 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/January 1996/97 were Germany with 26,948 tonnes whites against 35,841 tonnes and France with 7,859 tonnes, down from 14,187 tonnes.
